title: Affine Hom scheme for a finite locally free group source
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means a group object in schemes over $S$, and a homomorphism preserves multiplication, identity and inverse. Let $D$ and $G$ be $S$-group schemes, with $D\to S$ finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and $G\to S$ affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and of finite presentation. Here finite presentation means locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The functor on $S$-schemes $T$ given by $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{T\text{-gp}}(D\times_ST,G\times_ST)$ is represented by an affine $S$-scheme $B$ of finite presentation: there are bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{T\text{-gp}}(D\times_ST,G\times_ST)$ natural in every $T$. Fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]. No smoothness, Noetherianity or reducedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Write $D^2=D\times_SD$. Its first projection to $D$ is a base change of $D\to S$, hence finite locally free by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-base-change]. Composing with $D\to S$ and applying [lem-trf-finite-locally-free-composition] shows $D^2\to S$ is finite locally free. The identity $S\to S$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, directly from the identity ring map. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-fp-relative-hom-scheme] to $(X,Y)=(D,G),(D^2,G),(S,G)$ to obtain affine finitely presented $S$-schemes $H,K,L$, respectively. For every $T/S$ their points are ordinary maps $D_T\to G_T$, $D_T^2\to G_T$, and $T\to G_T$, respectively. Each application uses precisely the finite locally free source and the given affine finitely presented target $G$.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3, printed pp.58-59, and Exercise 2.4.5, printed p.77; explicit group-operation fibre products. Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For $u:D_T\to G_T$, define two $K(T)$-points $a_T(u)=u\circ m_D$ and $b_T(u)=m_G\circ(u\times_Tu)$, and two $L(T)$-points $c_T(u)=u\circ e_D$ and $d_T(u)=e_G$. Multiplication and identity are taken after base change to $T$. All four rules commute with pullback: the induced map of fibre products has the prescribed projections, and composition of pulled-back maps is the pullback of composition. Thus [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], applied in schemes over $S$ and using the natural bijections of step 1, gives $S$-morphisms $a,b:H\to K$ and $c,d:H\to L$. This uses exactly the fully faithful form of Yoneda, not a claim about an arbitrary presheaf.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3, printed pp.58-59, and Exercise 2.4.5, printed p.77; explicit group-operation fibre products. Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Set $M=K\times_SL$, $v=(a,c):H\to M$, $w=(b,d):H\to M$, and form $B=H\times_{(v,w),M\times_SM,\Delta_M}M$. These schemes and maps exist by [def-pc-fibre-product]; the diagonal is the pair of identity maps. Its universal property gives a bijection between maps $T\to B$ over $S$ and maps $u:D_T\to G_T$ satisfying $u m_D=m_G(u\times_Tu)$ and $u e_D=e_G$. Indeed the additional $M(T)$-point in the fibre product is forced to be $v(u)=w(u)$; it adds no choice. This description commutes with every $T'\to T$ by the same universal property.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3, printed pp.58-59, and Exercise 2.4.5, printed p.77; explicit group-operation fibre products. Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$. By the explicit affine-chart conclusion of [lem-sfb-affine-fp-relative-hom-scheme], write $H_U=\operatorname{Spec}P$, $K_U=\operatorname{Spec}Q$, $L_U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $P,Q,C$ finitely presented $A$-algebras. The four arrows induce $\alpha,\beta:Q\to P$ and $\gamma,\delta:C\to P$. Choose finite algebra generators $q_i$ of $Q$ and $c_j$ of $C$, and set $J=(\alpha(q_i)-\beta(q_i),\gamma(c_j)-\delta(c_j))\subset P$. For an $A$-algebra $R$, a map $P\to R$ kills $J$ exactly when its composites with each pair agree on generators, hence on every polynomial in those generators and on all elements of $Q,C$. It therefore gives precisely the points of $B_U$ in step 3. The affine spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies these with maps to $\operatorname{Spec}(P/J)$. This identification holds for all $U$-schemes: on an affine open cover use the just-proved formula; uniqueness on affine opens covering each overlap, followed by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], glues the maps in both directions. Thus $B_U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(P/J)$. If $P=A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$, lift the finitely many generators of $J$ to polynomials $s_1,\ldots,s_t$; then $P/J=A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m,s_1,\ldots,s_t)$. All index sets here are finite.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3, printed pp.58-59, and Exercise 2.4.5, printed p.77; explicit group-operation fibre products. Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Step 4 says that the inverse image of every affine open of $S$ is affine, so $B\to S$ is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. The displayed finite presentation gives local finite presentation at every point by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), the affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; hence it is of finite presentation in the sense of the statement. No finite affine cover of $S$ and no Noetherian hypothesis was used.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3, printed pp.58-59, and Exercise 2.4.5, printed p.77; explicit group-operation fibre products. Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Finally the multiplication and identity equations in step 3 force preservation of inverses. For every $T$-scheme $V$ and $x\in D_T(V)$, the equation $x x^{-1}=1$ gives $u(x)u(x^{-1})=1$ in the group $G_T(V)$, so $u(x^{-1})=u(x)^{-1}$. Equality on all such points implies equality of the two scheme morphisms by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. Conversely a group homomorphism satisfies both imposed equations by definition. Thus step 3 gives exactly the natural bijections required in the statement, and step 5 supplies their affine finitely presented representative. These constructions also work over the empty base; for the trivial group $D=S$ the identity equation leaves only the identity section, so $B=S$.
